deep.reconstruction:
PURPOSE. The page states, without proof, two-sided asymptotic Diophantine-approximation results for x = e^{2/a}, where a is a nonzero integer. Write {y} = y - [y] for the fractional part. The quantity 1+[y]-y = 1-{y} is the distance from y up to the next integer. A marginal note says: 'See Q. 784(ii) in volume. This goes further.' This points to Ramanujan's problem 784 in the Journal of the Indian Mathematical Society; the page is a sharpened version of it.

CLAIMS ON THE PAGE. Throughout, epsilon > 0 is arbitrary.

I. For any integer a:
 (1) {N e^{2/a}} < (1+eps) loglogN/(|a| N logN) for infinitely many N.
 (2) {N e^{2/a}} > (1-eps) loglogN/(|a| N logN) for all N > delta(eps).

II. For a even:
 (3) 1-{N e^{2/a}} < (1+eps) loglogN/(|a| N logN) for infinitely many N.
 (4) 1-{N e^{2/a}} > (1-eps) loglogN/(|a| N logN) for all large N.

III. For a odd:
 (5) 1-{N e^{2/a}} < (1+eps) loglogN/(4|a| N logN) infinitely often.
 (unnumbered) 1-{N e^{2/a}} > (1-eps) loglogN/(4|a| N logN) for all large N.

In short:
- a even: both one-sided liminfs of N logN/loglogN times the distance equal 1/|a|.
- a odd: the 'from below' side has constant 1/|a| and the 'from above' side has constant 1/(4|a|).

METHOD (from the next folio; reconstructed and checked by me).
- Start from tanh(1/a) = 1/(a+1/(3a+1/(5a+...))). Then X := (e^{2/a}+1)/2 = 1/(1-tanh(1/a)).
- For a>0 this gives X = [1; a-1, 3a, 5a, 7a, ...]. For a<0 it gives X = [0; 1, |a|, 3|a|, ...].
- Convergents u_n/v_n satisfy u_1=v_1=1, u_2=|a|, v_2=|a-1|, and w_{n+1} = (2n-1)|a| w_n + w_{n-1}.
- Then X - u_n/v_n is approximately ±1/(v_n v_{n+1}) and v_{n+1} ~ 2|a| n v_n. Also log v_n ~ n log n, so n ~ logN/loglogN.
- Hence |v_n X - u_n| ~ 1/(2|a| n v_n).
- Since e^{2/a} = 2X - 1, the case N = v_n gives N e^{2/a} - (2u_n - N) ~ ±loglogN/(|a| N logN).
- When v_n is even, take N = v_n/2. This gives N e^{2/a} - (u_n - N) ~ ±loglogN/(4|a| N logN).
- The lower-bound ('for all N') halves need in addition the standard fact that convergents give the best approximations, a Davis-type argument. Ramanujan does not supply this here.

PARITY ANALYSIS (mine).
- If a is even, v_2 = |a-1| is odd and v_{n+1} ≡ v_{n-1} (mod 2). So every v_n is odd, the sign alternates, and I and II follow.
- If a is odd, v_{n+1} ≡ v_n + v_{n-1} (mod 2) with v_1 = 1 and v_2 even. The parities are therefore 1,0,1,1,0,1,1,0,... with period 3: v_n is even exactly when n ≡ 2 (mod 3).
- Ramanujan's next page instead asserts that v_n is even exactly for n even. That is wrong, and the annotator of the previous folio flags exactly this ('v_5 even?').
- The even-denominator indices n = 2, 5, 8, ... alternate in parity, so the sign (-1)^{n-1} takes both values on them.
- Consequently, for odd a, approximations with constant 1/(4|a|) occur on both sides of the integers.
errors: Claim I(2) is false for odd a. For odd a, the denominators v_n are even exactly when n ≡ 2 (mod 3), not when n is even. These indices carry both signs, so {N e^{2/a}} < (1+eps) loglogN/(4|a| N logN) for infinitely many N.
Example for e^2 (a=1): the convergent 133/18, with next partial quotient 18, gives 18e^2 - 133 ≈ 0.0030 > 0. This is an even denominator on the 'fractional part small' side.
Corrected statement for odd a: both one-sided constants equal 1/(4|a|). Claims (1), (5) and the unnumbered lower bound in III remain true; (2) does not.

The underlying slip is Ramanujan's parity claim on the next page ('if a is odd and n is even, v_n is even'). The parity pattern actually has period 3; the annotator on the previous folio already noticed this ('v_5 even?').

For negative a, X = [0; 1, |a|, 3|a|, ...]. The convergent u_1/v_1 = 1/1 then lies above X, so the sign (-1)^{n-1} in (9) on the next page is reversed. This does not affect the corrected symmetric statements but shows the sign bookkeeping was not checked for a < 0.
The 'for all N > delta' lower bounds require the best-approximation property of convergents and control of intermediate fractions. These are asserted without proof (minor gap).

results.what: Exact one-sided rates: liminf N logN/loglogN · ||N e^{2/a}|| equals 1/|a| on each side for a even, and 1/(4|a|) for a odd (the page has the odd case only half right).
results.modern_name: Exact irrationality measure / Davis-type theorem for e^{2/a} (rational approximation of e^{2/a} with loglog q/(q^2 log q) accuracy)
results.usually_credited_to: C. S. Davis (1978) for e (constant 1/2); extensions to e^{2/a} and the analysis of this very manuscript by B. C. Berndt, S. Kim, A. Zaharescu (Adv. Math., c. 2013)

results.what: Continued fraction (e^{2/a}+1)/2 = [1; a-1, 3a, 5a, ...] derived from Lambert's continued fraction for tanh
results.modern_name: Lambert/Euler continued fraction for tanh, regular CF of e^{2/a}

deep.surprise_reason: This manuscript is known and has been analysed in print (Berndt–Kim–Zaharescu, around 2013). Davis-type rates for e were published in 1978, so Ramanujan anticipating them is notable but already documented. The parity error for odd a is the main point of interest.

checkable.asserts: ≈ 0.00301 > 0: an even N (=v_5/2 for a=1) with small positive fractional part, contradicting claim (2) for a=1 asymptotically.
Small negative value: N = v_8/2 = 23922 gives the 'from above' approximation with constant ~1/4, on the opposite side from N=18.
Regular CF of e^2, showing the large quotients 18, 30 attached to the even denominators 18 and 23922.
